title: Distribution Transformers: Fast Approximate Bayesian Inference With On-The-Fly Prior Adaptation

split.decision: Training: original 20 epochs of 100 batches of 5000 fresh synthetic problems from InverseGamma(4,6) meta-prior; BENCH_SEED determines model and training RNG. Validation: one public draw seed 20261029, 1000 problems. Hidden evaluation: five independent secret-seeded draws of 1000 problems each, preserving original Monte Carlo protocol and draw positions 3-7 while replacing public seeds for isolation. Input contains supplied prior parameters and observation, never latent variance or posterior samples.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 1, Experiment 4.1, DT-2 wide meta-prior; reproduced metric 0.005802714172750712

allowed_changes: The shared inference architecture, fitted representation, offline training method, training surrogate and optimizer may change; a Transformer is not mandatory.

When retaining the supplied DT training pipeline, changing only epochs=20, steps_per_epoch=100, batch_size=5000, warmup_epochs=5, lr=0.005, weight_decay=0 or use_prior_loss=true does not count as a method improvement.
Changing only the width or depth in `transformer_kwargs` (num_layers=6, d_model=64, n_head=8, dim_feedforward=256) also does not count.
fixed_contract: Improve prior-flexible amortised two-component approximation to the specified inverse-gamma posterior.
The supplied prior/observation distribution, normal likelihood, latent variance and log-variance output space are fixed.
Inference is amortised across problems; output is exactly two valid Gaussians. The original posterior KL Monte Carlo formula, Jacobian and aggregation remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not replace the Bayesian problem, fit each evaluation problem separately, run a posterior-sampling chain, expand the mixture family, change KL scoring, access labels or transfer information across evaluation problems.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.

evidence.finding: The score rule explicitly requires amortised inference and two components.
Amortised inference transfers expensive optimization to offline training and applies a learned mapping across tasks and priors.
